title: EU VAT Invoice Requirements 2026 Guide | Fakturcho
description: EU VAT invoice rules under Directive 2006/112/EC: mandatory fields, deadlines, credit notes, reverse charge, EN 16931, Peppol and ViDA e-invoicing from 2030.
h1: What must an EU VAT invoice contain?
answer: Under Council Directive 2006/112/EC (Article 226), an EU VAT invoice needs a date, sequential number, both parties' details, the supplier's VAT number, a description of goods or services, taxable amount, VAT rate and amount, or the exemption/reverse-charge wording. Intra-EU invoices are due by the 15th of the next month. From 2030, e-invoicing becomes mandatory for cross-border B2B supplies EU-wide.

sections.heading: What are the mandatory fields on an EU VAT invoice? (Article 226)

inline.text: Every EU business that charges VAT follows the same rulebook: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, the "VAT Directive," which sets minimum invoice content, issue deadlines, and required wording for corrections and exempt or reverse-charged transactions. Member states can add local requirements (numbering, currency, language, e-invoicing platforms) on top of this floor — see the country-specific guide for local rules and e-invoicing mandates.
Article 226 of Directive 2006/112/EC lists the details a full VAT invoice must contain:

inline.text: These points define a full invoice. A member state can require extra local fields (company registration number, capital, bank IBAN, etc.).

blocks.text: What content does a simplified invoice need? (Article 226b)

inline.text: Under Article 220a, member states must allow a simplified invoice when the amount is no more than

(or the national-currency equivalent), for a document treated as an invoice under Article 219 (corrections), or for suppliers using the small-enterprise exemption. A higher threshold needs an individual EU derogation under Article 395 — not a general range. A simplified invoice under Article 226b needs only:

items.text: date of issue;
identification of the supplier;
identification of the type of goods or services supplied;
the VAT amount payable, or the information needed to calculate it;
for a corrective document, a specific and unambiguous reference to the invoice it amends.

sections.heading: When must an EU invoice be issued?

inline.text: For an intra-Community supply of goods (Article 138), or a supply where the customer accounts for VAT under reverse charge (Article 196),
Article 222
currently requires the invoice
no later than the 15th day of the month following the month the chargeable event (the supply) occurred.
Domestic deadlines for purely local supplies are left to each member state.
This deadline shortens under ViDA: from
1 July 2030
, once Digital Reporting Requirements apply, Article 222 requires these invoices within
10 days of the chargeable event
(or of payment on account), and summary invoices within 10 days of the calendar month's end.

sections.heading: What wording do reverse charge and intra-Community exemptions need?

inline.text: Two situations require a specific legal reference on the invoice, not just an omitted VAT line:

items.text: Reverse charge (Article 196):
cross-border B2B service supply, customer accounts for VAT — invoice must state that fact, in practice "reverse charge," plus, where used, a reference to Article 196. No VAT amount is shown.
Intra-Community supply of goods, VAT-exempt (Article 138):

goods dispatched to a taxable person in another member state, exempt at origin — both parties' valid VAT numbers required, plus a note referencing the exemption (commonly "intra-Community supply, Article 138 Directive 2006/112/EC"). Supplier must also file an EC Sales List; since Directive (EU) 2018/1910, a missing or incorrect VAT number or Sales List entry can forfeit the exemption.

sections.heading: How do you correct an invoice or issue a credit note?

inline.text: The Directive has no separate "credit note" category: Article 90 requires the taxable amount to be reduced on cancellation, refusal, total or partial non-payment, or a price reduction after supply, under conditions each member state sets. Article 219 treats any document that specifically and unambiguously amends an earlier invoice as an invoice in its own right — it must carry the same mandatory content and cross-reference the original invoice number. National law sets the exact form.

A proforma (or quote) is not a VAT invoice under the Directive: it does not trigger the chargeable event, does not need a sequential number, and does not entitle the recipient to deduct VAT. It becomes an invoice only once reissued with the mandatory Article 226 content after the supply.

is the European semantic standard for electronic invoicing, developed by CEN under Directive 2014/55/EU. It defines the business terms a "core invoice" must carry, independent of file syntax (compliant syntaxes: UBL and UN/CEFACT CII). Since 2019, all EU public-sector contracting authorities must be able to receive EN 16931-compliant e-invoices.
Peppol

(Pan-European Public Procurement OnLine) is the delivery network built on that standard: a "four-corner" model where supplier and customer each connect through their own accredited Peppol Access Point, with no direct link needed between the parties. Many national e-invoicing mandates route documents over Peppol using an EN 16931-based national spec (a "CIUS").

sections.heading: What is ViDA and when do its e-invoicing rules apply?

inline.text: The Council adopted the
VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA)
package on 11 March 2025; it entered into force on 14 April 2025. Milestones:

head: Date
What changes
rows: 14 April 2025
ViDA enters into force; member states may introduce a domestic e-invoicing mandate without a Council derogation
1 July 2028
Single VAT Registration pillar: extended One-Stop-Shop scope, mandatory reverse charge for certain non-established suppliers
1 July 2030
Digital Reporting Requirements make structured e-invoicing mandatory for intra-EU B2B and mandatory-reverse-charge transactions
1 January 2035
Member states with a pre-existing domestic real-time reporting system must align it with the EU model

inline.text: The 1 July 2030 change is more than a reporting rule — ViDA rewrites four Directive articles:

items.text: Article 217:
only a structured, machine-readable format counts as an "electronic invoice."
Article 218(3):
EN 16931 (with the syntaxes under Directive 2014/55/EU) becomes the reference format.
Article 232:
a recipient can no longer refuse an EN 16931-compliant e-invoice in scope of the new digital reporting rules.
Article 226:
gains two new mandatory fields — a reference to the invoice being corrected, and the supplier's bank/virtual account number.

sections.heading: Checklist: before you send an EU B2B/B2C invoice

items.text: Sequential, unbroken invoice number
Date of issue and date of supply (if different)
Your VAT number and registered details
Customer's VAT number (mandatory for reverse charge and intra-Community supplies)
Description, quantity, unit price and VAT rate per line
Taxable amount and VAT amount per rate, or the exemption/reverse-charge reference
For intra-EU B2B supplies: issued by the 15th of the month after the supply
Corrections issued as a credit/debit note cross-referencing the original invoice number
Check whether your country already mandates a structured e-invoice format for this transaction

faq.question: Does every EU invoice need a QR code or digital signature?

answer.text: No — the VAT Directive does not require one. Some member states add extra requirements (QR code, software certification, real-time reporting) on top of Article 226; that is a national rule, not EU-wide.

faq.question: Can I issue an invoice in a foreign currency?

answer.text: Yes. The Directive allows any currency, but the VAT amount payable must also be expressed, or convertible, in the national currency where the tax is due, at an official rate.

faq.question: Is a proforma invoice enough to prove a sale for VAT purposes?

answer.text: No. A proforma carries no legal VAT invoice number and does not itself trigger VAT chargeability or a deduction right. A genuine invoice must follow once the goods or services are supplied.

faq.question: What happens if I get an intra-Community invoice wrong?

answer.text: Since Directive (EU) 2018/1910 amended Article 138, a missing or invalid customer VAT number, or a missing/incorrect EC Sales List entry, can forfeit the zero-rate exemption — the supplier can become liable for the VAT.

faq.question: Do I need to mention "reverse charge" in a specific language?

answer.text: The Directive requires the fact to be stated, not fixed wording in a fixed language; most member states expect their own official language or accept "reverse charge" in English.

faq.question: Will I have to send e-invoices to every EU customer soon?

answer.text: From 1 July 2030, Digital Reporting Requirements make structured e-invoicing mandatory for intra-EU B2B transactions. Before that date, obligations depend on your country's domestic mandate (see the table above) — several already require it earlier.

faq.question: What is the difference between EN 16931 and Peppol?

answer.text: EN 16931 is the semantic content standard — what data an invoice must contain and mean. Peppol is the delivery network and technical spec used to transmit that structured invoice between accredited providers. Last reviewed: 25.09.2026. This page is general information, not tax or legal advice — confirm your own obligations with your tax authority or accountant.
